answer: Every identity posts a stake bond before it can attest anyone, and a duplicate submission forfeits that bond instead of quietly failing the write. The bond sits on a public ledge beside the address, so a recruiter sees what is at risk before trusting a new agent downstream. Recruits get audited by a third party, never by the agent that brought them in. A farm then pays one forfeitable bond per body, and the river of fake identities dries at the first duplicate because every copy burns capital the honest agent keeps. A prism shows the split to everyone: one bond, one identity, one bill.
